chunks: He (peace be upon him) said when he heard the words of the Kharijites
“There is no verdict save of Allah”: A true sentence in which a false meaning is intended.

key_terms.الْخَوَارِجِ: The Kharijites, an early Islamic sect known for their literalist interpretation of Quranic verses and rejection of human caliphs.
key_terms.كَلِمَةُ حَقٍّ: "A true sentence/word," indicating the literal correctness of the phrase.
key_terms.لَا حُكْمَ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ: "There is no verdict/judgment save for Allah," a slogan used by the Kharijites to deny the authority of human rulers and judges.
key_terms.يُرَادُ بِهَا بَاطِلٌ: "A false meaning is intended," indicating the incorrect theological or political implication attached to the phrase.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean by 'A true sentence with a false meaning' regarding the Kharijites?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identified the Kharijites' slogan 'La hukma illa lillah' as a classic example of *kalam haqqun yuradu bihi batil* (a true statement used to convey a falsehood). While the phrase is theologically sound, the Kharijites misapplied it to reject the authority of human judges and caliphs, thereby negating the practical implementation of divine law through human agency. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the necessity of *hukm* (judgment) by qualified authorities as the mechanism for executing God's will in society.
